title: One shape,
subtitle: three recipes.
summary: How every Fizlet piece is written, the bricks to pick for each use, and three recipes that run on the page: an action, a shooter and two players.
lead: Everything built on Fizlet has the same shape: one root, one engine, state in typed arrays, and systems that measure in `read`, simulate in `step` and write in `render`. Learn the shape once and every brick fits it. The three recipes below are complete: each one runs on this page as written, and each shows the size it ships, measured on this build.

items.title: A root
items.body: One element the piece lives in. The engine pauses when it scrolls away, the HUD finds its readouts inside it, and nothing is drawn outside it.

items.title: An engine
items.body: `createEngine({ root, seed })`. Add `settle: 0.5` for anything that should cost nothing while it's still, `fps: 30` for an ambient loop.

items.title: State in typed arrays
items.body: Positions, timers and scores in `Float64Array`s made once. The step reads and writes numbers only, so nothing is allocated while it runs.

items.title: read, step, render
items.body: Measure the page in `read`. Simulate in `step` at a fixed 60 Hz, with no DOM at all. Draw and write the page in `render`, through `engine.ledger`.

items.title: Events for effects
items.body: The step emits what happened (`e.events.emit("hit", …)`); render, sound and the HUD react to the ring. The sim never knows about pixels or audio.

items.title: A way out
items.body: Bind your own listeners to `e.signal`. `e.destroy()` then removes them all and gives back every page change: [Recall](/docs/recall/).

blocks.heading: Pick bricks by use
blocks.subhead: Start from the kernel and add only what the job needs; each brick is its own import and its own budget.

items.title: A reaction on the page
items.body: A click, a hover, a scroll that should feel alive: `fzlt/fx` for particles, `fzlt/timeline` for choreographed DOM moves, `fzlt/hud` for counts. Settle on.

items.title: An arcade game
items.body: `fzlt/input` (and `fzlt/pad` on touch), `fzlt/collide`, `fzlt/fx`, `fzlt/hud`; `fzlt/rules` for waves, drops and score; `fzlt/match` for start, pause and results; `fzlt/arcade` when the page itself is the board.

items.title: Two or more players
items.body: A deterministic step and `fzlt/presence`: inputs in lockstep, a state hash every 30 frames. `syncCheck` proves it in a test; the rooms server joins two devices.

items.title: A hero in an Astro slot
items.body: `fzlt/slot` loads the scene near the viewport and keeps the slot's text alternative; `fzlt/camera` pans and zooms a DOM stage.

blocks.heading: Recipe 1: an action
body: A real button on the page, a burst of sparks out of it on every click, and a count. The canvas is added through the ledger, the class through `ledger.cls`, the count through `fzlt/hud`, so `destroy()` leaves the button as it was. Half a second after the last spark, the engine settles: no frames at all until the next click. With reduced motion it counts without the burst.
blocks.caption: Click **Like**. The sparks are pooled (cap 160); a full pool refuses new ones instead of growing.

blocks.heading: Recipe 2: a shooter
body: Bugs fall; you move and fire. Every bug and shot is a slot in a typed array, spawns come from the seeded `e.random` (the same seed plays the same wave), hits are `circles` tests in the step, and the blast and the shake happen in render from the event ring. The engine runs only between **Start** and the last life, so the page's own keys stay the page's.
blocks.caption: **Start**, then A/D or ←/→ and Space. On a phone, drag to move and tap to fire.

blocks.heading: Recipe 3: two players
body: Two peers on one page, each with its own engine, controls and screen, joined by `memory()`: an in-memory link with three ticks of latency and jitter. Only inputs cross it, 12 bytes a message. Each sim runs a frame only when both inputs for it are in, so both screens show the same game, and the hash check every 30 frames says so. Swap `memory()` for `join(url)` and the same code plays across two devices through a [room server](/guides/multiplayer-rooms/).
blocks.caption: Player 1: A/D. Player 2: J/L. On touch, hold the left or right half of a screen. The frame count only moves when both inputs are in.

items: **Measure it.** Bundle, minify and gzip your piece; that is what a visitor downloads. The badges above are measured that way on every build.

**Check the step.** No `Math.random`, no clock, no layout reads, nothing allocated. [Determinism](/docs/determinism/) and the [contract](/docs/contract/) list the rules; `fzlt/debug` counts layout reads in a step.
**Check Recall.** Snapshot the page, run the piece, `destroy()` it, and compare: the DOM should match.
**Check stillness.** With `settle`, a piece that is not moving should ask for no frames. The [perf overlay](/bricks/perf.html) shows it.

seo.title: Authoring with Fizlet: the shape and three recipes
seo.description: How to write any Fizlet piece, which bricks to pick by use, and three recipes that run as is: an action on the page, a shooter and two players, measured.
